title: LadybugDB - Embedded Columnar Graph Database
description:
Kuzu, with 10+ enterprise customers and VLDB publications, was acquired by Apple. Teams using embedded graph databases for agentic AI are now scrambling for a replacement.
### Development Halted
Kuzu's open source development stopped post-acquisition. No new features, bug fixes, or community support.
### Security Risk
Unpatched vulnerabilities and no path forward for critical security updates. Your data deserves better.

## LadybugDB: The only viable successor
Built on battle-tested foundations with a commitment to open source. LadybugDB carries forward the Kuzu vision with active development and enterprise support.
### 10x Faster Queries
Columnar storage with vectorized execution delivers lightning-fast analytical queries on graph data.
### Embedded & Serverless
Zero external dependencies. Run anywhere - edge, embedded, or cloud. Perfect for agentic applications.
### Columnar Storage
Optimized for analytics on connected data. Compress better, scan faster than traditional graph stores.
### Enterprise Support
Commercial support contracts available. Backed by a team committed to long-term development.

MIT
Open source license, forever
> The Kuzu team set a high bar in graph databases with their research innovations described in publications at leading conferences such as VLDB, making it easy to deploy anywhere with a fast Cypher query engine and a permissive license for use in highly regulated industries. Ladybug is committed to maintaining that bar with a low barrier to entry.

## Production-ready in 3 steps
From installation to querying your graph in under 5 minutes.
1
### Install
One command installation via curl or Homebrew. No dependencies, no configuration needed.
`brew install ladybug`
2
### Connect
Import your data using Cypher queries or one of our language SDKs (Python, Node.js, Rust).
`CREATE (n:Entity {name: 'Alice'})`
3
### Query
Run analytical queries with Cypher. Leverage columnar storage for complex agg/egations.
`MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN n, r, m`

Join the teams building the future of agentic AI on LadybugDB. No credit card required. Open source forever.

title: Ladybug: The Next Chapter for Embedded Graph Databases
description:
# Ladybug: The Next Chapter for Embedded Graph Databases
It's with deep gratitude for the amazing product the #KuzuDB team created, and a mix of necessity and excitement, that I announce the launch of Ladybug. This is a new open-source project and a community-driven fork of the popular embedded graph database.
Last Friday, the [Kuzu](https://ca.linkedin.com/company/kuzu-inc?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-mention) Git repository was archived, leaving a gap for many users and developers. Since then, members of the community and I have been exploring ways to ensure this important work continues. That's why we're launching Ladybug—to carry the #KuzuDB legacy forward and evolve it into the "DuckDB for graphs."
### Why Ladybug, and Why Now?
My commitment to this fork is driven by over 15 years of experience building large-scale infrastructure at companies like Facebook and Google. In that time, I’ve learned that companies prioritize simplicity and scale, often giving up on semantics. However, to truly solve business problems holistically, they also require an understanding of relationships and semantics. I am convinced that graph technology, when done right, is the key to aligning these three needs: Semantics + Simplicity + Scale. After an extensive search for the best technology foundation, I believe the #KuzuDB approach was exactly that—and now, with Ladybug, we are taking that vision forward.

Our initial focus is on stabilizing the code base and storage engine. Beyond that, our ambitious roadmap includes:
- Fixing bugs, with immediate priority on any security issues.
- Building out robust lake house functionality, allowing direct table creation on object storage without an initial ingest step.
### Who is Behind Ladybug?
This effort is led by [ Arun Sharma ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arundsharma?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-mention) (Me!), serving as the Project Lead and focusing on development and the lake house architecture. I bring a decade of experience supporting the OSS Linux Kernel development and a deep background in infrastructure engineering to ensure Ladybug adheres to the highest open-source standards and governance.

title: Ladybug: Spreading its Wings
description:
If you are a Kuzu user, it is high time you migrate to its vibrant successor, LadybugDB.
Since Kuzu was officially archived in October 2025, our team forked the repository to ensure the graph database ecosystem continues to thrive under **LadybugDB** with fixing security vulnerabilities and integrating with other data storage systems as a major focus. Over the last few months, we have introduced a massive array of features, performance improvements, and ecosystem expansions that make the [v0.15](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/releases/tag/v0.15.0) release our biggest milestone yet
So what’s new?
## Massively Expanded Ecosystem
We’ve invested heavily in making LadybugDB accessible from anywhere. We now offer first-class bindings for the following languages:
- Python (support for Python 3.14!)
- Node.js
- Rust
- WebAssembly (Wasm) [Try it in your browser](https://ladybugdb.github.io/wasm-shell/)
- Java
- Go
- Swift
- V-lang
- Julia
- Ruby (community)
- Nim (community)
For a deep dive into using these APIs, check out our [Client APIs Documentation](https://docs.ladybugdb.com/client-apis/).

Full support for seamlessly integrating **Arrow**, **DuckDB**, and **Parquet** datasets is here. Rather than migrating or converting your external data into native Ladybug tables, you can simply attach these databases and query them directly!
Here is how you can use an Arrow source transparently as a node table:
```
CREATE NODE TABLE Employee (id INT64, name STRING, PRIMARY KEY (id))
WITH (storage='arrow://my_arrow_table_id');
```

## Subgraph Support
Creating and querying multiple graph namespaces just got a whole lot easier with true subgraph support. You can now define isolated graphs and switch contexts natively:
```
CREATE GRAPH my_graph;
USE my_graph;
```
You can also CREATE and MERGE nodes without creating a node table first
```
CREATE GRAPH my_graph ANY;
USE my_graph;
CREATE (u:User {name: 'Alice'});
```

We aren’t stopping at v0.15. Here’s a quick peek at what’s coming next:
- **Native SQLite Support**: Seamless querying across SQLite natively in LadybugDB
- **Advanced Arrow & Parquet Optimizations**: Execution layer enhancements to handle even larger, more complex queries over columnar formats efficiently
- **Improved Compatibility with other Graph Databases**: Multi-label support for ANY type graphs without compromising the strict schema and typing

title: GitHub - LadybugDB/ladybug: LadybugDB a graph database
description:
Ladybug is an embedded graph database built for query speed and scalability. Ladybug is optimized for handling complex analytical workloads on very large databases and provides a set of retrieval features, such as a full text search and vector indices. Our core feature set includes:
- Flexible Property Graph Data Model and Cypher query language
- Embeddable, serverless integration into applications
- Native full text search and vector index
- Columnar disk-based storage
- Columnar sparse row-based (CSR) adjacency list/join indices
- Vectorized and factorized query processor
- Novel and very fast join algorithms
- Multi-core query parallelism
- Serializable ACID transactions
- Wasm (WebAssembly) bindings for fast, secure execution in the browser
Ladybug is being developed by [LadybugDB Developers](https://github.com/LadybugDB) and is available under a permissive license. So try it out and help us make it better! We welcome your feedback and feature requests.
The database was formerly known as [Kuzu](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu).
## Installation
| Language | Installation |
|---|---|
| Python | `pip install ladybug` |
| NodeJS | `npm install @ladybugdb/core` |
| Rust | `cargo add lbug` |
| Go | `go get github.com/LadybugDB/go-ladybug` |
| Swift | [lbug-swift](https://github.com/LadybugDB/swift-ladybug) |
| Java | [Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.ladybugdb/lbug) |
| C/C++ | [precompiled binaries](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/releases/latest) |
| CLI | [precompiled binaries](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/releases/latest) |
